sections.html: Greetings in French depend on time of day and formality. France and Québec both value politeness: always greet someone (in a shop, an elevator, an office) before asking anything.

sections.heading: Saying hello
sections.html:
French Meaning When to use
Bonjour Hello / Good morning / Good day Default, any time until evening, formal or informal
Bonsoir Good evening From about 6 pm
Salut Hi / Bye Informal: friends, family, people your age
Coucou Hey there Very informal, friends/family, texts
Allô Hello On the phone (in Québec also used informally in person)

sections.heading: Saying goodbye
sections.html:
French Meaning
Au revoir Goodbye (neutral, polite)
À bientôt See you soon
À plus tard / À plus / À+ See you later (informal)
À demain See you tomorrow
À tout à l'heure See you later today
Bonne journée Have a good day
Bonne soirée Have a good evening
Bonne nuit Good night (going to bed)
Salut Bye (informal)
Bonne fin de semaine (Québec) / Bon week-end (France) Have a good weekend

sections.heading: Asking how someone is
sections.html:
Formal Informal
Comment allez-vous ? Comment vas-tu ? / Comment ça va ? / Ça va ?

Answers: - Très bien, merci. Et vous ? — Very well, thank you. And you? - Ça va bien. — It's going well. - Pas mal. — Not bad. - Comme ci, comme ça. — So-so. - Pas très bien. — Not very well.

sections.heading: Tu or vous?
sections.html:
• tu — one person you know well: friend, family member, child, classmate.
  • vous — someone you don't know, someone older, a professional situation, or more than one person (always).
  • When unsure, use vous. The other person may say On peut se tutoyer ("We can use tu").
  • In Québec, tu is used much more readily than in France.

sections.heading: Polite expressions
sections.html:
• S'il vous plaît (formal) / S'il te plaît (informal) — Please
  • Merci (beaucoup) — Thank you (very much)
  • De rien / Je vous en prie (formal) / Bienvenue (Québec) — You're welcome
  • Excusez-moi / Pardon — Excuse me
  • Enchanté(e) — Nice to meet you

sections.heading: Physical greetings
sections.html:
• La bise (kisses on the cheeks) among friends and family in France: usually 2 kisses, varies by region. In Québec, often 2 kisses among friends; handshakes are standard in professional settings.
  • Une poignée de main (handshake) for formal and first meetings.

sections.heading: Example dialogue
sections.html: — Bonjour madame, comment allez-vous ? — Très bien, merci. Et vous ? — Bien, merci. … — Au revoir, bonne journée ! — Merci, vous aussi !

exercises.prompt: It is 8 pm. You enter a restaurant. What do you say?
Formal or informal? (a) *Salut* (b) *Comment allez-vous ?* (c) *Coucou* (d) *Je vous en prie*.
You will see your colleague again this afternoon. How do you say goodbye?
Translate: "Hi, how are you? — Not bad, and you?" (informal)
exercises.answer: *Salut, ça va ? — Pas mal, et toi ?*
